authorization.initial: Owner approved USD 1 / 40 total HTTP requests, no activation or deployment.
authorization.extension: Owner explicitly approved 66 total HTTP requests for fifteen corrected cases, reusing three unchanged paid results; USD 1 total unchanged; no activation or deployment.

fixture_correction: The initial run included synthetic source-kind/observation inconsistencies introduced by the agent. All original inputs and outcomes remain preserved; no qualification is inferred from superseded inputs. Fifteen corrected cases were evaluated once; three unchanged fixture/request hashes were reused.

validation_correction.reason: The new configuration-prescription regex matched across clauses and fields, rejecting bounded code-fix verification using comparable capture/sampling. Four Red regressions proved this; matching is now confined to a single field and clause. Direct configuration/suppression prescriptions remain rejected. No prompt or provider request bytes changed.
validation_correction.offline_replay: All eighteen final paid responses validate unchanged against their exact fixture/request hashes after the clause-boundary fix; both no-request cases abstain. Replay made no HTTP requests.

reviewer: Codex manual review of every final retained response, deterministic plans and the recorded released baseline. Scores are agent judgement; no human acceptance is claimed.
summary: All reviewed final text is evidence-linked and safety-compatible. Seventeen paid cases reach 7/8 or better; the overlapping-health response is repetitive (6/8), adds little to factual plans and regresses against the retained health baseline. Both no-request abstentions are correct. Keep the changed profile unqualified; do not lower the rubric or spend beyond the approved cap.

comparison.deterministic_plans: The main product improvement is reliable configuration-aware planning with observed policy/rule/alert/diagnostic state, separate control effects and verification; this works without AI. Several provider responses add source-specific cache/refresh, shipping-step or request-reproduction questions, but that gain is not consistent across health cases.
comparison.released_baseline: Historical provider results only, not a newly purchased controlled A/B. Reliability, privacy and measured flow retain safe next steps; full-mode retry contrast is less explicit and overlapping-health guidance is weaker. No universal quality or no-regression claim is made.

remaining_work: Improve full-mode evidence-specific and health investigation wording, while preserving allowed reference groups and avoiding repeated generic checks.
Run a newly authorised bounded qualification for any changed provider request hashes; existing receipts may only be reused for exactly unchanged inputs.
Owner review/testing and separate release/activation authorisation remain outstanding.

investigations.title: Investigate recurring checkout submission timeouts
checks: Inspect the linked incident and recurrence evidence alongside the authorised checkout execution path; distinguish the recorded linkage from evidence of a shared cause.
Reproduce the timeout after retry and test any explanation against the retained observations before making a bounded change.

Add a regression check for the same failure path, then verify current recovery and recurrence through comparable observations and capture settings. A quiet period or resolved status alone does not establish a fix.

cases.review: Uses the recorded incident/recurrence group and checkout retry symptom; asks for reproduction and a regression check without asserting a common cause. The retained released baseline has a sharper with/without-retry comparison; this is useful but not an across-the-board quality improvement.

investigations.title: Review background refresh warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context to determine whether cache misses are expected and whether users are affected; the occurrence count is lifetime evidence, not a period total.
Check the refresh behaviour against both an expected cache miss and a genuine failure to distinguish routine context from an unexpected condition.
If an unexpected behaviour is changed, compare subsequent observations under similar traffic and verify that genuine failures and useful diagnostic context remain visible.

cases.review: Uses the cache-miss/background-refresh symptom and contrasts expected refresh behaviour with genuine failure before any tuning. Server controls own the configuration choices and their separate effects.

investigations.title: Review repeated request failures
checks: Inspect retained request-failure evidence to establish response semantics, expected behaviour and user impact; recurrence alone does not establish harmless noise.
Check whether the observed behaviour is expected or unexpected, and whether retained context is redundant or diagnostically useful.

After any bounded change, observe comparable traffic and reproduce both the expected pattern and a genuine failure. Verify useful context and regression visibility remain, and revert if evidence is lost.

cases.review: Asks for response semantics, expected behaviour and user impact; does not classify recurrence or an unknown status as harmless noise.

investigations.title: Investigate authorization responses
checks: Inspect the retained failure evidence and authorized execution path to distinguish expected denials from broken access.
Reproduce the observed response and check whether access succeeds when authorization is expected.
If a bounded change is warranted, add a regression check and observe the same path under comparable traffic and capture settings; verify current recovery and recurrence.

cases.review: Distinguishes expected authorization denial from broken access by reproducing a path where authorization should succeed. It does not suggest suppression.

investigations.title: Investigate checkout submission timeout
checks: Inspect the retained incident evidence and authorised checkout submission path; attempt to reproduce the timeout after retry and test possible explanations against the observed behaviour.
Inspect retained alert delivery history to distinguish repeated notifications from distinct failures; the incident count represents lifetime occurrences, not the reporting period.

After a bounded change, add a regression check and observe the same failure path under comparable traffic and capture settings. Verify current recovery and recurrence, and confirm distinct critical failures remain visible and deliverable.

cases.review: Explicitly separates repeated notifications from distinct failures and lifetime counts from period activity. The server supplies observed cooldown/scope and delivery safeguards.

investigations.title: Review background refresh warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning evidence to determine whether the cache miss is expected, redundant, or associated with user impact; check for evidence that could disprove each possibility.
Inspect current matching rules and effective capture coverage, including any unobserved local settings, before interpreting missing evidence.

If an unexpected behavior is changed, reproduce the warning pattern and a genuine failure, then compare subsequent observations under comparable traffic. Confirm diagnostic context and regression visibility remain available.

cases.review: Checks current matching rules and coverage before interpreting missing evidence. The server, rather than provider prose, identifies the already-enabled demotion and its distinct usage effect.

investigations.title: Review background refresh warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context to determine whether cache misses during background refresh are expected and whether users are affected.
Compare the expected refresh pattern with genuine failures to check whether the warning indicates unexpected behaviour or redundant context.
If a bounded correction is warranted, verify it against comparable traffic and check that genuine failures and useful diagnostic context remain visible.

cases.review: Checks expected versus user-impacting refresh behaviour. The server identifies the expired rule and requires rechecking scope; the provider does not presume an expired rule is effective.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache-miss warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context and background refresh evidence to determine whether the cache miss is expected, redundant or associated with user impact.

Check whether the expected refresh pattern and genuine refresh failures can be distinguished in the retained evidence; inspect current matching rules and note that SDK-local settings have not been observed.

If unexpected behavior is changed at its source, reproduce the expected pattern and a genuine failure, then compare subsequent observations under comparable traffic. Verify useful context and regression visibility remain; revert if evidence is lost.

cases.review: Uses the refresh symptom, inspects matching rules and explicitly acknowledges unobserved SDK-local settings. Requires preserving failure/regression visibility after a source fix.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache-miss warnings

Check whether the expected refresh pattern and a genuine failure can be distinguished in the retained evidence.
If unexpected behavior is changed, reproduce both patterns and compare subsequent observations under comparable traffic; verify useful context and genuine failures remain visible.

cases.review: Compares expected refresh behaviour with genuine failure. The server supplies the verbose sensitivity snapshot and warns that discovery volume is distinct from reliability.

investigations.title: Review background refresh cache warnings
checks: Inspect retained warning context and related refresh outcomes to determine whether cache misses are expected and whether users are affected.
Compare an expected refresh pattern with a genuine failure to check whether the warnings distinguish useful diagnostic evidence from repeated context.
If unexpected behaviour is corrected, reproduce both patterns and review a subsequent comparable observation for regressions and preserved failure visibility.

cases.review: Provides a symptom-specific expected-versus-genuine-failure comparison. The server supplies the active probe/diagnostic check and requires preserving evidence still needed for investigation.

investigations.title: Review the background refresh warning
checks: Inspect retained warning evidence to determine whether the cache miss is expected, redundant or associated with user impact; the occurrence count reflects lifetime observations, not the supplied period.
Compare expected refresh behavior with a genuine failure to check whether the warning distinguishes routine misses from unexpected behavior.
If an unexpected behavior is corrected, reproduce both patterns and review a subsequent comparable observation for preserved diagnostic context and failure visibility.

cases.review: Makes no claim to have inspected a repository or SDK hook. The server keeps SDK settings unobserved and requires separately authorised inspection before any consumer change.

investigations.title: Investigate shipping-step drop-offs
checks: Inspect the recorded analysis window, funnel denominator, sampling, instrumentation and shipping flow; compare device segments where captured to determine whether the pattern is consistent.
Reproduce the affected flow and check whether any observed obstacle accounts for the drop-offs; absence of an obstacle would weigh against that explanation.
If a bounded change is warranted, add a regression check and compare subsequent observations using equivalent sampling, denominator and capture policy; missing data does not establish improvement.

cases.review: Checks the shipping flow, actual denominator, sampling and captured device segments; explicitly asks whether reproducing an obstacle accounts for drop-offs and treats absence as contrary evidence.

investigations.title: Investigate shipping-step drop-offs
checks: Inspect the funnel denominator, sampling, instrumentation and partial coverage for the recorded analysis window; compare device segments and trace the affected flow.
Reproduce the shipping flow to identify where sessions leave and check whether the measurements reflect actual abandonment.

If evidence supports a bounded change, add a regression check and compare subsequent observations using equivalent sampling, denominator and capture policy; verify any coverage changes before interpreting the comparison.

cases.review: Checks partial coverage, denominator and instrumentation before interpreting abandonment; any change is conditional on evidence, with comparable subsequent measurement. It does not claim a measured conversion loss from incomplete data.
cases.false_positive_match: change, add a regression check and compare subsequent observations using equivalent sampling

investigations.title: Investigate checkout submission timeouts

investigations.title: Investigate shipping-step drop-off
checks: Inspect the funnel denominator, sampling, instrumentation, affected flow and comparable device segments. Check the recorded incident linkage without assuming a shared cause.
Reproduce the affected flow before choosing a bounded change; add a regression check and compare subsequent observations with equivalent sampling, denominator and capture policy.

cases.review: Keeps the incident and flow as separate investigations and explicitly avoids assuming a shared cause from the recorded link. Reliability precedes the flow check.
cases.false_positive_match: change; add a regression check and compare subsequent observations with equivalent sampling

investigations.title: Investigate the open critical incident
checks: Inspect the retained incident evidence and authorised execution path; determine what the recorded recurrence represents without treating the lifetime count as a period total.
Attempt to reproduce the observed failure and test any explanation against the available evidence.
Verify any bounded change with a regression check and a subsequent comparable observation. Check current recovery and recurrence; a quiet period or resolved status alone does not establish a fix.

cases.review: Appropriately stays at the permitted critical-incident signal level, without withheld English or multilingual identity. Reproduction, lifetime-count caveat and comparable recovery/recurrence checks are useful within restricted disclosure.

investigations.title: Review the recurring background task warning

Compare an expected task run with a genuine failure to identify whether the warning reflects unexpected behaviour.

After any bounded change, use a regression check and comparable observations of the same failure path to verify recovery and recurrence; a quiet period or resolved status alone is insufficient.
